faq.a: Nurcan is associated with the Arabic form نُورْجَان, whose core sense is nurcan; light soul (turkish).

faq.q: What is the origin of Nurcan?
faq.a: Nurcan is associated with Arabic. Nurcan is a Turkish compound of Arabic نُور (nūr, 'light') + can ('soul').
Yes — the underlying form نُورْجَان is Arabic.
Nurcan can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Nurcan should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Nūr occurs in the Quran as a term for light.

faq.q: What does Nurcan mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Nurcan is rendered نور جان and carries the sense نور جان، نور کی روح.

faq.q: What does Nurcan mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Nurcan is rendered نورجان and carries the sense نورجان، جان نور.
A romanized syllable approximation is nur-can. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Nurcan?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Nurcan, nurcan. Script forms are نور جان, نورجان, نُورْجَان, नूरजान.

faq.q: Is Nurcan a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
